For the polar curve $r=\frac{{e}^{2\theta }}{2\pi },$ calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ as a function of $\theta .$

| $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ | $=$ | {{field-1}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | $2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ |
worked_solution:
To find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use the formula for differentiating parametric curves:

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )}
$$

First, we recall that to convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

Using the fact that $r=\frac{{e}^{2\theta }}{2\pi },$ we get

$$
x=\frac{{e}^{2\theta }}{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\frac{{e}^{2\theta }}{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

To compute our derivative, we first need to calculate ${x}^{′}(\theta )$ and ${y}^{′}(\theta ).$ 

- First, we compute the derivative of $x$ with respect to $\theta $ using the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(\theta ) & ={(\frac{{e}^{2\theta }}{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }{({e}^{2\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }[({e}^{2\theta })^{′}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +{e}^{2\theta }\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{′}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }[2{e}^{2\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +{e}^{2\theta }\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )] \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }[2{e}^{2\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -{e}^{2\theta }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ] \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2\theta }}{2\pi }(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute the derivative of $y$ with respect to $\theta $ using the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\theta ) & ={(\frac{{e}^{2\theta }}{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }{({e}^{2\theta }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }[({e}^{2\theta })^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +{e}^{2\theta }\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{′}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }[2{e}^{2\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +{e}^{2\theta }\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )] \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }[2{e}^{2\theta }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +{e}^{2\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ] \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2\theta }}{2\pi }(2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )} \\  & =\frac{\frac{{e}^{2\theta }}{2\pi }(2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}{\frac{{e}^{2\theta }}{2\pi }(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$
